assessments.reasoning: GNU 1.3 [17885,19211) supplies the first-notice conditions, identifies the particular holder, reaches prior notices for any work and measures cure from receipt. The surrounding paragraphs distinguish the cessation route and the status of recipients.

challenge.method: Changed the work while keeping the notifying holder the same, then changed the holder. Tested cure just before and exactly at the 30-day threshold. Checked the adjacent provisions for recipients and reacquisition.
challenge.results: An earlier qualifying notice from the same holder concerning another work defeats first-notice status. An earlier notice solely from a different holder does not. Receipt starts the clock. Cure just before the threshold meets the timing condition, while cure at the threshold misses it. Termination of the licensee’s rights leaves recipients’ licenses intact under this clause. Receiving the material again gives the terminated licensee no rights to use it while permanent reinstatement is lacking.

limitations: Receipt, notice history, holder identity and effective cure require evidence. The scoped reference to a GNU FDL violation is governed by §9’s reference to this license. The passage does not resolve how to classify every notice involving a different edition.
reasoning: GNU 1.3 §9 provides permanent reinstatement from the notifying holder when that holder gives reasonable notice, this is the licensee’s first received violation notice under this license from that holder across all works, and cure occurs before 30 days have elapsed after receipt.
